Luciana, we have your quote for the four hospitals. The work is excellent, but the price is fifteen percent above our budget.
I understand, Ryan. What exactly does your budget cover? Installation only, or also maintenance?
Installation and one year of maintenance. And our clients want a service-level agreement with a response in four hours.
Four hours is fine. If you sign for three years, we will include the first year of maintenance at no extra cost.
That helps, but three years is a big commitment for us. Can you give us a discount on the installation?
Here is a counteroffer. If you change the payment terms to thirty days, we can reduce the installation by five percent.
So five percent, plus the maintenance. That is close. What is your bottom line?
That is our best offer. If you meet us halfway on the payment terms, we will send the new quote today.
What exactly does your budget cover?

I have trained negotiators for twenty years, and I teach one rule before all the others. Never give anything for free. When a client asks for a discount, many people simply say, OK, five percent. That is a mistake. The client learns that your first price was not real, and next week he asks for more. So every concession needs a condition. The sentence is simple: if you do this, we will do that. If you sign today, we will give you five percent. If you pay in advance, we will include the training. You are still flexible, but the client always gives something back.

Thank you for your interest in our cameras. Let me explain our prices, because they depend on the volume. For five hundred cameras, the price is ninety dollars per camera. If you order more than one thousand, the price will go down to seventy-five dollars. Our payment terms are thirty percent in advance and seventy percent on delivery. The price covers the cameras and the software license for the first year. Maintenance is not included, but if you sign a three-year contract, we will send an engineer to Brazil for the installation at no extra cost. Unless you confirm by the end of the month, these prices may change.

People think a hospital only wants the lowest price. That is not true. When I read a quote, I do not look at the price first. I look at the service-level agreement. If a camera stops in the emergency room, how fast will the supplier come? In a hospital, four hours can be too long. I also prefer long contracts, because changing suppliers in a hospital is expensive and risky. In my last negotiation, I accepted a higher price. Why? Because the supplier offered a response in two hours, and a three-year commitment. If a supplier understands that, we will meet halfway very quickly.
